美和神社は[[甲府盆地]]東部に位置し、町域北西部の二ノ宮地区に鎮座する。古代甲斐国においては盆地中央北縁にあたる笛吹市春日居町に前期[[国府]]が所在し、笛吹市御坂町国衙近辺に移転したと考えられている。御坂町域は亀甲塚古墳や[[姥塚古墳]]など古墳時代の中小古墳や二之宮遺跡などの集落遺跡が分布し、古代には国衙関係の遺構や史跡が分布している。 律令制下では山梨郡井上郷に比定され、「二ノ宮」は国衙にも近接し美和神社に由来する。近世には二之宮村が成立し、美和神社を中心としてきた。二ノ宮地区に所在する美和神社は[[里宮]]として位置付けられており、二ノ宮から東に位置する尾山地区には[[山宮]]として杵衡神社がある。 == 歴史 == 美和神社は[[三輪山]]を[[神体]]とする[[大和国]]（[[奈良県]]）の[[大神神社]]から勧請され、尾上郷の杵衡神社へ遷された後に新たに二之宮に遷座されたとする伝承が一般的で、『[[甲斐国社記・寺記]]』や『[[甲斐国志]]』に拠れば、由緒は[[景行天皇]]のころ[[甲斐国造]]の[[塩海足尼]]が勧請を行ったといわれる。初見史料は『[[日本三代実録]]』[[863年]]（[[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]5年）6月8日条記事で、同日に美和神社は従五位に叙せられ、[[一条天皇]]から二宮の号を与えられたという。 中世には甲斐守護の[[武田氏]]からの崇敬を受け、[[1479年]]（[[文明 (日本)|文明]]11年）には[[信濃国]][[佐久郡]]領主[[大井氏]]が甲斐へ侵攻しているが、このときには美和神社も戦火に見まわれた。[[武田信虎]]期には[[山梨郡]]万力郷（現[[山梨県]]）に社領を寄進され、[[1557年]]（[[弘治 (日本)|弘治]]3年）には[[武田信玄|武田晴信]]（信玄）から条目を下され、[[浅間神社 (笛吹市)|浅間神社]]（笛吹市一宮町一宮）や三宮[[玉諸神社#玉諸神社 (甲府市)|玉諸神社]]（[[甲府市]]）、武田氏氏神の[[武田八幡宮]]（[[韮崎市]]）などとともに府中八幡宮（現甲府市の[[八幡神社 (甲府市宮前町)|八幡神社]]）への勤番役を免除されている。 [[1565年]]（[[永禄]]8年）6月には武田家嫡男の[[武田義信]]家臣による[[太刀]]奉納が行われている「甲州二宮造立帳」美和神社文書。『[[甲陽軍鑑]]』に拠れば前[[1564年]]（永禄7年）1月には義信家臣が謀反を企てたとして成敗されており、翌年の1565年（永禄8年）には義信自身も幽閉される義信事件が起こっているが、造立帳の記録から事件発覚は1565年（永禄8年）のことであるとも考えられている平山優「武田勝頼の再評価」『新府城と武田勝頼』（山梨県韮崎市教育委員会、2001年）。また、翌年の[[1566年]]（永禄9年）には義信生母でもある信玄正室の[[三条夫人]]が[[具足]]を奉納している。 [[1573年]]（[[元亀]]4年）9月11日には家督相続直後の[[武田勝頼]]が武運長久の祈祷を命じており、[[1579年]]（[[天正]]7年）には勝頼から禁制を下されている。武田氏滅亡後は、[[1582年]]（天正10年）には[[織田信長]]と[[織田信忠]]から禁制を下され、翌年の[[1583年]]（天正11年）には[[徳川家康]]から社領安堵を受け、[[1589年]]（天正17年）に[[伊奈忠次]]の行った[[検地]]で社領が確定する。豊臣系大名時代には[[加藤光泰]]や[[浅野氏]]から社領寄進を受けている。 神事として、戦国期から近世まで一宮と三宮の三社共同で竜王（[[甲斐市]]）の[[信玄堤]]で水防祈念を行う三社御幸（お御幸さん）が義務付けられており、4月の第三亥日には夏御幸、11月第二亥日には冬御幸が行われていた。明治期には三社御幸が禁止されたため毎年三月初申日に行われていた山宮御幸（二宮のお御幸さん）を4月15日に変更し春期例祭として位置づけ、戦後には一時期断絶したものの現在でも4月第一日曜に行われ、太々神楽の奉納が行われている。 また、毎年2月8日には[[湯立神事]]が行われる。美和神社の湯立神事は猿田彦の祈祷舞を伴い、県内で現存する唯一の湯立神事。地域に伝わる[[1826年]]（文政9年）の「社司年中行事吉令」によれば、二ノ宮の湯立は3月中旬の太々神楽とは別に2月8日に行われていた行事で、『[[裏見寒話]]』でも猿田彦の舞が記されている。 神主は坂名井家で、[[坂名井聡翁]]は国学者としても知られる。 == 文化財等 == [[ファイル:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|湯立神事での猿田彦の祈祷舞（2011年2月8日撮影）]] [[ファイル:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji A.JPG|thumb|250px|湯立神事での儀式（2011年2月8日撮影）]] [[ファイル:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji B.JPG|thumb|250px|笹の葉を沸騰したお湯に浸して参拝者にかける（2011年2月8日撮影）]] ;重要文化財（国指定） *彫刻 **木造大物主神立像 - [[1906年]]（明治39年）9月6日指定、平安時代の作品{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|2937|木造大物主神立像}}、2017年5月19日閲覧。{{PDFlink|[https://www.city.fuefuki.yamanashi.jp/documents/607/5bf21d9faea4d.pdf 笛吹市文化財ガイドブック]}} - 笛吹市、2019年12月23日閲覧。 ;山梨県指定有形文化財 *工芸品 **白糸威褄取鎧〈残欠〉 - [[1986年]]（昭和61年）3月19日指定、南北朝時代の作品{{Refnest|group="注釈"|甲冑研究家の三浦一郎は同鎧の製作年代について、その製法から、[[武田信成]]・[[武田信春|信春]]の時期を推定している三浦一郎『甦る武田軍団 その武具と軍装』[[宮帯出版社]]、2007年5月28日、p. 7 - 13。}} **朱札紅糸素懸威胴丸 佩楯付 - 1986年（昭和61年）3月19日指定、伝・武田信玄の元服鎧{{Refnest|group="注釈"|ただし三浦一郎は、同鎧はその形式からして信玄の元服した時期よりも新しい天正年間の作で、[[前田利家]]所用の金小札白糸素懸威胴丸具足（重要文化財・[[前田育徳会]]所蔵）など織豊政権下で活動した武将の甲冑との間に共通した製法や意匠が見られると評し、同鎧の実際の所用者を武田氏滅亡後に甲斐を治めた[[河尻秀隆]]かその周辺人物を推定している三浦一郎『甦る武田軍団 その武具と軍装』宮帯出版社、2007年5月28日、p. 13 - 19。なお、同鎧の左肩部分にある削ぎ落された箇所については、秀隆絶命時の刀疵の可能性も想定される。}} *絵画 **板絵著色三十六歌仙図 - [[1965年]]（昭和40年）8月19日指定、[[1563年]]（永禄6年）に武田信玄・義信父子が連名で寄進 ;山梨県指定無形民俗文化財 *二ノ宮美和神社の太々神楽 付版木1枚、神楽二十五番次第1枚 - [[1981年]]（[[昭和]]56年）3月12日指定、[[元禄]]年間に始まったといわれる ほか、[[神主]]である坂名井家には中世から近代に至る坂名井家文書が所蔵されており、平成21年には[[山梨県立博物館]]に収蔵された。 === 『天正年中二宮祭礼帳』 === 美和神社には『天正年中二宮祭礼帳』（『祭礼帳』）が伝来している平山（1999）、p.384。『祭礼帳』は全75丁で後欠、全体的に[[虫損]]が激しいことが指摘される。 社伝に拠れば[[1575年]]（天正3年）の成立とされ、記載される武田家臣の人名のうち、御蔵前衆・[[末木家重|末木淡路守]]（家重）は活動時期が永禄末期から天正期で、天正9年に隠居すると天正15年に死去している。また、天川兵部助・天川宮内助の両名は武田氏滅亡後に徳川氏に対して提出された[[天正壬午起請文]]に見られることから、社伝通りの天正年間の作成であると考えられている。 内容は戦国期における神事の日付や内容・負担者・費用等が記され、戦国期の神事の実態を知る史料として重視されている。 また、『二宮祭礼帳』には[[カツオ]]・うずわ（[[ソウダガツオ]]）・[[イワシ]]・[[アワビ]]など中世甲斐国における[[海産物]]の利用を記録していることも注目されている数野雅彦「山梨の食文化を記録した歴史資料について」『甲州食べもの紀行』、p.121。 == 美和神社の太々神楽 == 春期例祭において、氏子の美和神社神楽保存会の会員により宵宮と翌本祭に境内の神楽殿において上演される[[太々神楽]]。演目は素面・着面、一人舞や数人による舞、物語性の有無など多様な舞があり、斉場清浄の舞、建国の舞、四柱の舞、天下りの舞、四弓の舞、合舞、剣打の舞、保存神の舞、国向の舞、魚釣の舞、剣の舞、四剣の舞、宝環の舞、種下の舞、大蛇の舞、悪病除の舞、幸替の舞、天岩戸の舞、終止の舞の二十種が現存している。 当日午前中は少女たちによる[[浦安の舞]]が本殿で行われると御輿に御魂が遷され、尾上に向けて出発する。神楽は御輿が杵衡神社で神事を終えて帰還するまで続けられる。 地域に伝わる「当神楽再興申定」によれば、美和神社の神楽は江戸中期の[[1754年]]（宝暦4年）に本殿造営が行われた際に再興されたものであるという。美和神社文書に含まれる「神楽二十五番次第」は江戸後期の神楽次第であると考えられており、伊勢系の古い次第を多く含み、素面の舞が多いなど現在の演目とは隔たりがある。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} '''注釈''' {{draft}} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Miwa Shrine | image = [[File:Miwa shrine №2 Fuefuki-city.JPG|250px]]
Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Miwa Shrine''' (美和神社, Miwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Fuefuki, Yamanashi|ja|笛吹市|lt=Fuefuki City}}, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan. It is classified as a {{ill|Kokushi Genzaisha|ja|国史見在社}} and is the {{ill|Ninomiya|ja|二宮}} (second-ranked shrine) of Kai Province. Under the Modern Shrine Ranking System, it held the status of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deity == * {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} == Location == Miwa Shrine is located in the eastern part of the {{ill|Kōfu Basin|ja|甲府盆地}}, within the Ninomiya area in Misaka-cho. Historically, it was near the provincial capital of ancient Kai Province, evidenced by nearby archaeological sites and ancient structures. == History == Miwa Shrine is traditionally said to have been founded during the reign of Emperor Keikō, with its origins traced to the worship of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi}}, a deity associated with {{ill|Mount Miwa|ja|三輪山}}, Nara Prefecture. The shrine was later moved to its current location in Ninomiya. The earliest record of the shrine appears in the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (863 CE), which notes its elevation to Junior Fifth Rank. During the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|lt=Sengoku period}}, the shrine was revered by the Takeda clan, receiving land grants and other support from Takeda Shingen and his successors. After the fall of the Takeda, the shrine received protection under Oda Nobunaga, Tokugawa Ieyasu, and the feudal lords of the Edo period. == Cultural Properties == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] ;Important Cultural Property (National) * Wooden standing statue of Ōmononushi no Mikoto (Heian period) ;Yamanashi Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties * White-thread ceremonial armor (Nanbokuchō period) * Board painting of the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets (donated by Takeda Shingen and Takeda Yoshinobu in 1563) ;Yamanashi Prefecture Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property * Daidai Kagura of Miwa Shrine == Main Rituals == * **Yutate Ritual (February 8):** A traditional purification ritual involving boiling water and prayer dances performed by shrine priests. * **Spring Festival (April):** Features the performance of Daidai Kagura and a procession to a nearby auxiliary shrine. == References == * {{Cite book|title=Kai Province History|author=Horiuchi Shin|publisher=Yamanashi Historical Society|date=2003}} * Miwa Shrine Preservation Committee Documents == External Links == * [http://www.city.fuefuki.yamanashi.jp/kanko/shisetsu.php?id=83 Official Page of Miwa Shrine - Fuefuki City Tourism] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} == References == {{reflist}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} [[Category:{{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Original pages]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] }}]] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

{{draft}} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miwa Shrine | image = [[File:Miwa shrine №2 Fuefuki-city.JPG|250px]]
Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Miwa Shrine''' (美和神社, Miwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Fuefuki, Yamanashi|ja|笛吹市|lt=Fuefuki City}}, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan. It is classified as a {{ill|Kokushi Genzaisha|ja|国史見在社}} and is the {{ill|Ninomiya|ja|二宮}} (second-ranked shrine) of Kai Province. Under the Modern Shrine ranking System, it held the status of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined deity == * {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} == location == Miwa Shrine is located in the eastern part of the {{ill|Kōfu Basin|ja|甲府盆地}}, within the Ninomiya area in Misaka-cho. Historically, it was near the provincial capital of ancient Kai Province, evidenced by nearby archaeological sites and ancient structures. == History == Miwa Shrine is traditionally said to have been founded during the reign of Emperor Keikō, with its origins traced to the worship of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi}}, a deity associated with {{ill|Mount Miwa|ja|三輪山}}, Nara Prefecture. The shrine was later moved to its current location in Ninomiya. The earliest record of the shrine appears in the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (863 CE), which notes its elevation to Junior Fifth rank. During the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|lt=Sengoku period}}, the shrine was revered by the Takeda clan, receiving land grants and other support from Takeda Shingen and his successors. After the fall of the Takeda, the shrine received protection under Oda Nobunaga, Tokugawa Ieyasu, and the feudal lords of the Edo period. == Cultural Properties == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] ;Important Cultural Property (National) * Wooden standing statue of Ōmononushi no Mikoto (Heian period) ;Yamanashi Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties * White-thread ceremonial armor (Nanbokuchō period) * Board painting of the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets (donated by Takeda Shingen and Takeda Yoshinobu in 1563) ;Yamanashi Prefecture Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property * Daidai Kagura of Miwa Shrine == Main Rituals == * **Yutate Ritual (February 8):** A traditional purification ritual involving boiling water and prayer dances performed by shrine priests. * **Spring festival (April):** Features the performance of Daidai Kagura and a procession to a nearby auxiliary shrine. == References == * {{Cite book|title=Kai Province History|author=Horiuchi Shin|publisher=Yamanashi Historical Society|date=2003}} * Miwa Shrine Preservation Committee Documents == External Links == * [http://www.city.fuefuki.yamanashi.jp/kanko/shisetsu.php?id=83 Official Page of Miwa Shrine - Fuefuki City Tourism] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} == References == {{reflist}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} [[Category:{{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:original pages]] }}]] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Miwa Shrine''' (美和神社, Miwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Fuefuki, Yamanashi|ja|笛吹市|lt=Fuefuki City}}, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan. It is classified as a {{ill|Kokushi Genzaisha|ja|国史見在社}} and is the {{ill|Ninomiya|ja|二宮}} (second-ranked shrine) of Kai Province. Under the Modern Shrine ranking System, it held the status of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined deity == * {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} == location == Miwa Shrine is located in the eastern part of the {{ill|Kōfu Basin|ja|甲府盆地}}, within the Ninomiya area in Misaka-cho. Historically, it was near the provincial capital of ancient Kai Province, evidenced by nearby archaeological sites and ancient structures. == History == Miwa Shrine is traditionally said to have been founded during the reign of Emperor Keikō, with its origins traced to the worship of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi}}, a deity associated with {{ill|Mount Miwa|ja|三輪山}}, Nara Prefecture. The shrine was later moved to its current location in Ninomiya. The earliest record of the shrine appears in the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (863 CE), which notes its elevation to Junior Fifth rank. During the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|lt=Sengoku period}}, the shrine was revered by the Takeda clan, receiving land grants and other support from Takeda Shingen and his successors. After the fall of the Takeda, the shrine received protection under Oda Nobunaga, Tokugawa Ieyasu, and the feudal lords of the Edo period. == Cultural Properties == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] ;Important Cultural Property (National) * Wooden standing statue of Ōmononushi no Mikoto (Heian period) ;Yamanashi Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties * White-thread ceremonial armor (Nanbokuchō period) * Board painting of the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets (donated by Takeda Shingen and Takeda Yoshinobu in 1563) ;Yamanashi Prefecture Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property * Daidai Kagura of Miwa Shrine == Main Rituals == * **Yutate Ritual (February 8):** A traditional purification ritual involving boiling water and prayer dances performed by shrine priests. * **Spring festival (April):** Features the performance of Daidai Kagura and a procession to a nearby auxiliary shrine. == References == * {{Cite book|title=Kai Province History|author=Horiuchi Shin|publisher=Yamanashi Historical Society|date=2003}} * Miwa Shrine Preservation Committee Documents == External Links == * [http://www.city.fuefuki.yamanashi.jp/kanko/shisetsu.php?id=83 Official Page of Miwa Shrine - Fuefuki City Tourism] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} == References == {{reflist}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} [[Category:{{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:Pages from wikipedia]] [[Category:Pages_from_Simple_English_Wikipedia]][[Category:Pages_from_Simple_English_Wikipedia]] }}]] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

It is classified as a {{ill|Kokushi genzaisha|ja|国史見在社}} and is the {{ill|Ninomiya|ja|二宮}} (second-ranked shrine) of Kai Province. Under the Modern Shrine ranking System, it held the status of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined deity == * {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} == location == Miwa Shrine is located in the eastern part of the {{ill|Kōfu Basin|ja|甲府盆地}}, within the Ninomiya area in Misaka-cho. Historically, it was near the provincial capital of ancient Kai Province, evidenced by nearby archaeological sites and ancient structures. == History == Miwa Shrine is traditionally said to have been founded during the reign of Emperor Keikō, with its origins traced to the worship of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi}}, a deity associated with {{ill|Mount Miwa|ja|三輪山}}, Nara Prefecture. The shrine was later moved to its current location in Ninomiya. The earliest record of the shrine appears in the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (863 CE), which notes its elevation to Junior Fifth rank. During the {{ill|Sengoku period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|lt=Sengoku period}}, the shrine was revered by the Takeda clan, receiving land grants and other support from Takeda Shingen and his successors. After the fall of the Takeda, the shrine received protection under Oda Nobunaga, Tokugawa Ieyasu, and the feudal lords of the Edo period. == Cultural Properties == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] ;Important Cultural Property (National) * Wooden standing statue of Ōmononushi no Mikoto (Heian period) ;Yamanashi Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties * White-thread ceremonial armor (Nanbokuchō period) * Board painting of the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets (donated by Takeda Shingen and Takeda Yoshinobu in 1563) ;Yamanashi Prefecture Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property * Daidai Kagura of Miwa Shrine == Main Rituals == * **Yutate Ritual (February 8):** A traditional purification ritual involving boiling water and prayer dances performed by shrine priests. * **Spring festival (April):** Features the performance of Daidai Kagura and a procession to a nearby auxiliary shrine. == References == * {{Cite book|title=Kai Province History|author=Horiuchi Shin|publisher=Yamanashi Historical Society|date=2003}} * Miwa Shrine Preservation Committee Documents == External Links == * [http://www.city.fuefuki.yamanashi.jp/kanko/shisetsu.php?id=83 Official Page of Miwa Shrine - Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined Deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Pilgrimage (general)|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] {{draft}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miwa Shrine | image = [[File:Miwa shrine №2 Fuefuki-city.JPG|250px]]
Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined Deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:ファイル]] }}{{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] }}{{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miwa Shrine | image = [[File:Miwa shrine №2 Fuefuki-city.JPG|250px]]
Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] }}{{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miwa Shrine | image = [[File:Miwa shrine №2 Fuefuki-city.JPG|250px]]
Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:pages needing attribution]][[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[Category:pages needing attribution]] [[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:pages needing attribution]][[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[Category:pages needing attribution]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:properly attributed pages]][[category{Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] }}{{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

{{draft}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miwa Shrine | image = [[File:Miwa shrine №2 Fuefuki-city.JPG|250px]]
Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:properly attributed pages]][[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] }}{{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:properly attributed pages]][[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] [[Category:From Everybodywiki with needed marking of original title]] }}{{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代type制度}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories|[[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:properly attributed pages]][[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] [[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]] }}{{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}
