[[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miwa Shrine | image = [[File:Miwa shrine №2 Fuefuki-city.JPG|250px]]
Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miwa Shrine | image = [[File:Miwa shrine №2 Fuefuki-city.JPG|250px]]
Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901年}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48年}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58年}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901st year }}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48th year }} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58th year }}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社[[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]]) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901st year }}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48th year }} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58th year }}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48th year }} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58th year }}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miwa Shrine | image = [[File:Miwa shrine №2 Fuefuki-city.JPG|250px]]
Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine}} (美和神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜}} ({{ill|901|ja|901st year }}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48th year }} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58th year }}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{citation needed|Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories| }} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{afc comment|1=see [[every:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] [[Category:Unsorted]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New-]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:completion tier 2]] [[Category:pages which might possibly be incomplete but are most likely complete]] [[Category:I think I cleared all the incomplete or blank pages earlier]] }} [[en:draft:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] [[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] [[sn:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]]

It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮|12=draft}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県|12=draft}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|12=draft}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜|12=draft}} ({{ill|901|ja|901st year|12=draft}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府|12=draft}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平|12=draft}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒|12=draft}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服|12=draft}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久|12=draft}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺|12=draft}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺|12=draft}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=draft}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方|12=draft}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港|12=draft}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山|12=draft}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿|12=draft}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿|12=draft}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|12=draft}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48th year|12=draft}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58th year|12=draft}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿|12=draft}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門|12=draft}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造|12=draft}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛|12=draft}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)|12=draft}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん|12=draft}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!|12=draft}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社|12=draft}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線|12=draft}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス|12=draft}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス|12=draft}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ|12=draft}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)|12=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{citation needed|Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories| }} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{afc comment|1=see [[every:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] [[Category:Unsorted]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New-]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:completion tier 2]] [[Category:pages which might possibly be incomplete but are most likely complete]] [[Category:I think I cleared all the incomplete or blank pages earlier]] }} [[en:draft:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] [[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] [[sn:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]]

Haiden of Miwa Shrine | location = 1450-1 Ninomiya, Misaka-cho, Fuefuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35|37|47.74|N|138|39|12.84|E|region:JP-19|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto|12=draft}} | type = Kokushi Genzaisha (Shinto shrine listed in historical records), Ninomiya of Kai Province, Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Traditionally attributed to the era of Emperor Keikō | honden_style = Nagare-zukuri | festival = March 15 | rituals = Yutate Ritual (February 8) | map = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|ja|美和神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Miwa Shrine|12=draft}} (美和神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Japan]]. It is a [[Ninomiya (shrine)|Ninomiya]], or a second rank shrine in its province after the [[Ichinomiya]]. [[File:Miwa shrine Fuefuki-city.JPG|thumb|250px|Torii at Miwa Shrine (photo taken in April 2010)]] '''Misode Tenmangū''' (御袖天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} ({{ill|Tenman-gū|ja|天満宮|12=draft}}) located in {{ill|Onomichi, Hiroshima|ja|尾道市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|ja|広島県|12=draft}}. The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|12=draft}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜|12=draft}} ({{ill|901|ja|901st year|12=draft}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府|12=draft}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平|12=draft}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒|12=draft}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服|12=draft}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久|12=draft}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺|12=draft}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺|12=draft}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=draft}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方|12=draft}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港|12=draft}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山|12=draft}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿|12=draft}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿|12=draft}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|12=draft}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48th year|12=draft}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58th year|12=draft}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿|12=draft}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門|12=draft}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造|12=draft}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛|12=draft}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)|12=draft}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん|12=draft}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!|12=draft}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社|12=draft}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線|12=draft}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス|12=draft}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス|12=draft}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ|12=draft}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)|12=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{citation needed|Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories| }} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{afc comment|1=see [[every:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] [[Category:Unsorted]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New-]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:completion tier 2]] [[Category:pages which might possibly be incomplete but are most likely complete]] [[Category:I think I cleared all the incomplete or blank pages earlier]] }} [[en:draft:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] [[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] [[sn:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]]

The shrine's former ranking was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}. == Enshrined deity == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|12=draft}}, also known as Tenjin. == History == In the first year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜|12=draft}} ({{ill|901|ja|901st year|12=draft}}), the deity, during his lifetime, was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府|12=draft}} due to slander by {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平|12=draft}}. While traveling by ship, he landed at Onomichi, where locals served him barley rice and {{ill|reishu|ja|醴酒|12=draft}}. In gratitude, he tore a sleeve from his {{ill|kimono|ja|和服|12=draft}} and used it to depict his image, which he left with the locals. After his death (in the third year of Engi, 903), a small shrine was established during the {{ill|Enkyū|ja|延久|12=draft}} era (1069–1074) within the grounds of the temple Tenjinbō, to enshrine the "image on the sleeve," thus giving the shrine its name, Misode Tenmangū.{{Sfn|Shinto Encyclopedia|1936}} Tenjinbō later became {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺|12=draft}} and served as the shrine's {{ill|bettō|ja|別当寺|12=draft}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|12=draft}} reforms of the {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}. It remains adjacent to the shrine today. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=draft}}, the shrine was classified as a gōsha. There are numerous legends about Sugawara no Michizane's stops along the Seto Inland Sea in the {{ill|Chūgoku region|ja|中国地方|12=draft}}, with one version stating that a person named Kanaya hosted him. Some researchers suggest that the wealthy Kanaya family may have incorporated this narrative to emphasize their status. During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, particularly the early 19th century, the Kanaya family accumulated wealth from the thriving {{ill|Onomichi Port|ja|尾道港|12=draft}}. They commissioned noted scholars such as {{ill|Rai Sanyō|ja|頼山陽|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kan Chazan|ja|菅茶山|12=draft}} to write commemorative inscriptions for the shrine. The family also maintained barley fields used to brew reishu for the deity's reception. The family eventually disappeared, and the fields became overgrown by the mid-20th century.{{Sfn|Hiroshima Encyclopedia|1982}} == Festivals and Rituals == [[File:Miwa-shrine Yutateshinji Kagura.JPG|thumb|250px|Prayer dance during the Yutate ritual (photo taken on February 8, 2011)]] The "Tenjin Festival" is held over three days in mid-July (the weekend preceding July 25). Events include: - **Day 1:** A {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿|12=draft}} procession. - **Day 2:** Educational ceremonies, raffles, and entertainment performances. - **Day 3:** A concluding ceremony featuring the mikoshi ascending and descending the shrine's 55 stone steps during the "55-Step Daishinden Return Ceremony." == Shrine Buildings == The {{ill|honden|ja|本殿|12=draft}} is constructed in an {{ill|irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|12=draft}} style with copper roofing. The original structure was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|Shōwa 48 (1973)|ja|昭和48th year|12=draft}} and rebuilt in {{ill|Shōwa 58 (1983)|ja|昭和58th year|12=draft}}. The {{ill|haiden|ja|拝殿|12=draft}} also features irimoya-zukuri construction, and the main gate ({{ill|Shinmon|ja|神門|12=draft}}) is an eight-legged gate (hakkaku-mon) in a {{ill|kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造|12=draft}} style. == Grounds == The shrine's approach features 55 stone steps crafted from single slabs, with the last step intentionally joined from smaller stones. Nearby is a "resting stone" where the deity reportedly rested and a {{ill|sasuri-ushi|ja|さすり牛|12=draft}}, a rubbing ox statue believed to grant blessings. The shrine has been featured in various media. The steps were prominently shown in the film ''{{ill|Tenkōsei|ja|転校生 (映画)|12=draft}}'' and the drama ''{{ill|Teppan|ja|てっぱん|12=draft}}.'' The shrine grounds inspired the setting for ''{{ill|Kamisama no Memo-chō|ja|かみちゅ!|12=draft}},'' although its structures were modeled after {{ill|Ushitora Shrine|ja|艮神社|12=draft}} in the same city. == Access == - A 20-minute walk from {{ill|Onomichi Station|ja|尾道駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|San'yō Main Line|ja|山陽本線|12=draft}}. - A 5-minute walk from the "Nagasaiguchi" bus stop served by {{ill|Onomichi Bus|ja|おのみちバス|12=draft}} and {{ill|Chūgoku Bus|ja|中国バス|12=draft}}. - A 5-minute walk from the {{ill|Senkoji Ropeway|ja|千光寺山ロープウェイ|12=draft}} lower station. == Related Articles == * {{ill|Seichi junrei|ja|巡礼 (通俗)|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōyamadera|ja|大山寺 (尾道市)|12=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * ''Hiroshima Encyclopedia'' (広島県大百科事典〈下巻〉). Chūgoku Shimbun, 1982. == External Links == * [http://misodetenmangu.or.jp/ Official website of Misode Tenmangū] {{Shinto pilgrimage}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{commonscat|Miwa-jinja, Fuefuki}} {{citation needed|Miwa Shrine Fuefuki}} {{shinto-stub}} {{Draft categories| }} {{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{draft categories| }} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{afc comment|1=see [[every:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hiroshima]] [[Category:Tenman-gū shrines]] [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Onomichi]] [[Category:History of Onomichi]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fuefuki City]] [[Category:Kokushi Genzaisha]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[Category:Kai Province shrines]] [[Category:Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Intangible Cultural Heritage of Japan]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Miwa shrines]] [[Category:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] [[Category:Unsorted]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New-]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:completion tier 2]] [[Category:I think I cleared all the incomplete or blank pages earlier]] }} [[en:draft:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]] [[ja:美和神社 (笛吹市)]] [[ja:御袖天満宮]] [[sn:Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)]]
